scope: Proposition 13.6 (Terminal extension, uniformly in the initial spin law) of the manuscript “Critical mixing in the Sherrington–Kirkpatrick model” (preprints/Critical-mixing-in-the-Sherrington-Kirkpatrick-model-September-25-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 227 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 3ac6296cc238bae9), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 102. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: There are fixed T, C, c > 0 and disorder events of ordinary probability at least 1 − e−cn with the following property. For every matrix in these events, let X have any probability law on the cube, possibly depending on the matrix, and let the observation noises be independent of X. Set hT = TX + √ T g. The reference Gibbs law µhT has unscaled gap at least 1/2 except with probability e−cn. On the original spectral event choose a fixed c+ such that R = J + c+I ⪰ 0. For one further time unit add observations with drift RX and covariance rate R, obtaining hT+λ. Define the reference laws µh,λ(x) ∝ exp ( 1 − λ 2 xT J◦ x + hT x ) , 0 ≤ λ ≤ 1. The covariance and inverse unscaled gap of µhT +λ,λ are bounded by C, simultaneously in λ, outside an event of conditional probability e−cn, uniformly over the law generating X. At λ = 1 the reference law is product. These reference laws are the posteriors of the original Gibbs prior evaluated at the observations; no assertion about the posterior of the arbitrary law generating X is made.
